reading.body:
The clearest signal in this data is the shift from AI that answers questions to AI that takes actions, across software, browsers, and physical hardware, with most vendors headquartered in the United States and one each in Canada and France.

Six of the eight tools carry explicit notes about control, access, or safety risk. Devin holds full codebase access. Operator and Computer Use handle browser credentials and desktop systems. Figure AI and Physical Intelligence operate in physical environments where errors have physical consequences. That concentration of high-privilege, action-taking systems in a single category reflects where the frontier is moving: from inference to agency, and from bounded outputs to open-ended execution. Each step toward autonomy increases the compute load for inference, planning, and feedback loops, which in turn increases the power draw per task.

The two non-US entries are notable for what their notes emphasize. Cohere Command R+ is positioned around enterprise retrieval and data grounding. Mistral Large 2 is described as GDPR-first and sovereign, indicating that regulatory environment, not just technical capability, is shaping how frontier models are framed and deployed. The data does not include training compute, energy consumption, or data center locations, so no claim can be made about infrastructure footprint from this set alone. What it does show is the product surface of frontier AI as of mid-2026, weighted heavily toward autonomous action and physical embodiment, both of which place greater demands on the systems that run them.
